summary: This bill makes the Trump accounts contribution program permanent by removing its 2028 expiration date from the tax code, adds inflation adjustments to the $1,000 annual contribution limit after 2028, and updates related headings and references.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the tax code to make permanent and enhance a contribution program under IRC section 6434. This involves tax expenditures rather than direct appropriations or mandatory spending programs, so it has no direct bearing on government spending levels.

The legislation permanently extends and inflation-adjusts the Trump accounts contribution program in the Internal Revenue Code. This expands a tax-advantaged contribution mechanism, which constitutes a tax benefit and therefore pushes in the direction of lower taxes.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare coverage, insurance markets, or medical services.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not mention immigration, border policy, or pathways to citizenship.
No language pertains to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill makes no changes to defense authorizations or military spending.
No environmental regulations, energy policy, or climate provisions are present.
While the accounts may indirectly support long-term savings, the bill does not alter welfare programs, SNAP, Medicaid, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill does not address school funding, choice programs, or federal education policy.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The legislation contains nothing related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization measures are included.

Permanently extending a tax-advantaged contribution program will reduce federal revenue on an ongoing basis, increasing deficits relative to current law and therefore moving away from debt-reduction priorities.
The bill is silent on LGBTQ protections or related civil rights.
No foreign assistance or international aid provisions appear in the text.
The bill does not address voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight measures are present.
The legislation does not modify labor law, union rights, or workplace regulations.
No provisions concern religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
